title: The guest goes, and she stays sitting
note:
This key's one job is the ending. It used to double as the 'Lucy is too excited' de-escalation sheet, which is a different message; that fallback moved to door-sound-cover. So this is unambiguously a departure: he is going OUT, through the door, and she is staying.

Round 47 failed twice over. The leash hung as a loop from the handler's hand attached to nothing, exactly as round 33 of door-sound-05-settle did — the second time this has happened, so the clip is now described as an unbroken line from the D-ring rather than assumed. And Lucy was looking up at the handler instead of at the guest, which is the check-in read of door-sound-03-name; the post-mortems are explicit that a gaze needs the whole muzzle pointed at a named thing positioned relative to her head. Both are now in mustBeTrue, because the earlier version asked only that she stay sitting and the picture passed that while getting both wrong.
scene: Interior entry hall. The guest is stepping BACK OUT through the open front door — one foot already over the threshold onto the porch, his body turned to leave, with pale daylight and flat spruce foliage behind him — and he raises one hand in a small, unhurried goodbye wave. The guest wears the medium-blue zip-up hoodie, black baseball cap and clear-framed glasses from his likeness reference. He is NOT in a plaid or checked shirt — that was an earlier version of this character and is being replaced everywhere. He is plainly leaving, not arriving and not entering. Lucy SITS at the handler's side, square and settled, four paws on the floor. HER WHOLE MUZZLE POINTS AT THE DEPARTING GUEST, off to her right and across the frame from her, head level rather than tilted up: she is watching him go, without rising, leaning or straining toward him. She must NOT be looking up at the handler's face — a dog checking in with her handler is door-sound-03-name, a different picture, and this one is about her staying settled while someone leaves. THE LEASH IS ATTACHED TO LUCY: its metal trigger clip is closed around the D-ring at the FRONT of her collar, under her chin, and the black line runs continuously from that ring up to the handler's hand beside her, hanging in a slack curve on the way. Follow the line with your eye from her collar to her hand without a break. The leash must NOT hang as a loop from her hand attached to nothing. Give the leash a thin lighter outline where it passes near her coat and keep it off her back.
mustBeTrue: the leash is visibly clipped to the D-ring at the front of Lucy's collar and runs unbroken from there to the handler's hand in a slack curve, never hanging from her hand attached to nothing; the guest is unmistakably on his way out — a foot across the threshold, body turned toward the porch, hand raised in a small wave — and Lucy stays sitting at the handler's side with her whole muzzle pointed at the departing guest rather than up at the handler, and has not got up to follow him.
